(2026)", "metaDescription": "An honest, side-by-side comparison of Kodely and Bolt.new — pricing, code ownership, hosting, security and who each is best for.", "targetKeyword": "kodely vs bolt.new", "category": "Comparisons", "bodyHtml": "

Kodely and Bolt.new both let you describe a web app in plain English and watch real code get generated in front of you. That is where the similarity ends. They are built for different jobs, and picking the wrong one will waste your time either way. Here is a straight comparison, including where Kodely is behind.

TL;DR verdict

CategoryKodelyBolt.new
OutputReal Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 app, built from a hand-built component foundationFull-stack apps across several frameworks, run in-browser via WebContainers
Backend / databaseNot yet — frontend onlyYes, including database and auth integrations (e.g. Supabase)
Pricing modelMetered credits from actual AI cost; failed builds are never chargedSubscription tiers with monthly token allotments
Code accessView and copy source files in-app; no zip export yetFull project export and GitHub sync
Going liveOne-click publish to a free <name>.kodely.site URL, includedDeploy integrations to third-party hosts
Custom domainsNot yet — subdomain onlySupported through deploy integrations
Editing modelChat only, with free rollback checkpointsChat, plus direct code editing in the IDE

Short version: if you want a real, inspectable frontend up on a public URL in minutes with pricing you can actually predict, Kodely is built for that. If your project needs a database, authentication, or server logic today, Bolt.new is the more complete tool right now.

Pricing and credit model

Kodely gives you 750 credits free on signup, no credit card required. After that you top up as needed: $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (the most popular tier), or $90 for 6,000 credits. Credits never expire. A first build typically runs 100–150 credits, and a follow-up change is usually in the same range — so 750 free credits covers several real builds before you need to pay anything. The part that matters most: if a build fails to compile, Kodely attempts one automatic repair and does not charge you for the failure. You only pay for output that actually works.

Bolt.new runs on subscription tiers with monthly token allowances. That works well if your usage is steady, but it means you are paying for a plan whether you build once this month or twenty times, and token consumption on complex full-stack generations can be harder to predict up front than a flat per-build credit cost.

Do you own the code?

This is the sharpest difference between the two tools today. In Kodely, every generated file is real TypeScript and JSX — you can open the code view and see and copy any component. What you cannot do yet is export the whole project as a zip or push it to your own Git repository. If you need to take the raw project files and run them somewhere else, Kodely is not there yet.

Bolt.new supports full project export and GitHub sync, so if portability out of the tool is a hard requirement, that is a real advantage for Bolt.new.

Hosting and going live

Kodely publishes with a single click to a live, public URL at <yourproject>.kodely.site. It is free, included in every plan, and there is no separate hosting step to configure. There are no custom domains yet — you are on the kodely.site subdomain. For anyone who wants to go from idea to a working, shareable link without touching a hosting dashboard, this is Kodely’s biggest practical edge.

Bolt.new does not host for you directly — you deploy through integrations to outside hosting providers, which gives you more control over where the app ends up (including custom domains), at the cost of an extra step.

Backend depth: the honest gap

We are not going to dress this up. Kodely generates a real frontend application only — no backend, no database, no authentication, no payments. If your project needs any of that, Kodely cannot build it for you today. Bolt.new has real depth here: it supports full-stack generation with database and auth integrations, which makes it the more capable tool for anything beyond a frontend or a marketing site.

If your project is a landing page, a portfolio, a marketing site, a prototype, or any interface-first idea, this gap does not matter to you. If it needs user accounts or stored data on day one, it does — and Bolt.new is the better fit until Kodely closes that gap.

Security

Every project Kodely publishes is scanned for accidentally-leaked secrets and API keys before it goes live, so a hardcoded key in a generated file gets caught before it reaches a public URL rather than after. It is a narrow but concrete protection built specifically around Kodely’s one-click publish flow.

Best for

Choose Kodely if you want a real, readable frontend codebase, a live public link in one click, and pricing where you never pay for a broken build. Choose Bolt.new if your app needs a backend, database, or auth from the start, or if exporting the full project is a requirement.

FAQ

Can I move a Kodely project to my own hosting later?

Not today. You can view and copy individual source files from the in-app code view, but there is no full-project export yet.

Does Kodely support databases or logins?

No. Kodely currently generates frontend-only applications. If your app needs a backend, Bolt.new is the more complete option right now.

What happens if my Kodely build fails?

Kodely automatically attempts one repair. If the build still fails to compile, you are not charged credits for it.

Is Kodely free to try?

Yes — you get 750 credits on signup with no credit card required, enough for several real builds before any payment is needed.

Can I use a custom domain with Kodely?

Not yet. Published projects live on a free <name>.kodely.site subdomain.

Ready to see the difference yourself? Start building free on Kodely, or check pricing if you want the credit breakdown first.
